problem: The text says 'The flux linking the coil is B A cos ωt' and then 'Flux linkage changes as cos ωt', but the emf formula uses N turns. A student can lose track of where N comes from: BA cos ωt is the flux through one turn, while the flux linkage of the whole coil is N times that.
fix: Say: flux through one turn φ = B A cos ωt; flux linkage λ = N φ = N B A cos ωt; then e = −dλ/dt = N B A ω sin ωt, so E<sub>m</sub> = N B A ω.

problem: 'Half-cycle average: use in rectifier calculations' is vague and can mislead. A half-wave rectified sine has full-cycle output average Vm/π ≈ 0.318Vm, not 0.637Vm; 0.637Vm is the half-cycle average of the original sine (and the full-cycle average only of a full-wave rectified sine).
fix: Write: half-cycle average = 2Vm/π = 0.637Vm is the average of the original sine over one half cycle; a full-wave rectified sine keeps this value, while a half-wave rectified sine has average Vm/π ≈ 0.318Vm.
